question: What is the ruling on: inference proxy is a rules stack landed?
why_it_blocks: answered before the question door existed; migrated into the corpus so the system reads its Q&A in one place
answer:
ALL CALLS GO THRU INFERENCY PROXY, I BELIEVE CALLED "inference_domain". NO OTHER REACHING FOR INFERENCE VIA ANY OTHER MECHANISM IS ALLOWED. THAT NEEDS TO BE IN THE BUILD INSPECTION.
INFERENCE PROXY/INFERENCE DOMAIN is a rules stack. It's built with a "stack" for providers, listing their costs, connection handling, etc. Another "stack" for models. names, parameters, pros and cons, publish scores if any, etc. A 3rd "stack" for the provider/model combinations and what the specifics are. The fourth "stack" is the nest. a mesh built of seives that allow out the lowest cost answer. And the lowest cost answer is NEVER 127.0.0.1. It's hostname is Hex (or hex.local?), the Apple M1 Studio 32. That's what the inference proxy should usually route to, with failovers to Ollama Cloud Service, and Google Gemini. We have OpenRouter, but I shut it off because bugs kept sucking up all the cash. That's why we now have Hex.
no that's it. that's been the intention all along. we had some intentions and built many things. but clearly not to that level.
we can use nomic, but only to train graph trees learning words and bigrams. we want to be able to generate embeddings from those. so go ahead and get nomic for it as part of that.
Ruling IS settled
